explain.say: High in the stratosphere, mostly 15 to 35 kilometres up, there is a layer rich in ozone, a form of oxygen with three atoms instead of two. It acts as Earth's sunscreen.

explain.say: Ozone in turn absorbs harmful ultraviolet light and breaks apart, turning that energy into heat. The pieces rejoin, and the cycle repeats, so the shield keeps renewing itself.

explain.say: Without it, much more UV would reach the ground, causing sunburn and skin cancer and harming crops and plankton. Chemicals called CFCs thinned the layer, but since the 1987 Montreal Protocol phased them out it is slowly healing.

faq.a: Strong ultraviolet sunlight splits oxygen molecules, O2, into single oxygen atoms. Each atom then joins another O2 molecule to form ozone, O3.
When an ozone molecule absorbs ultraviolet light, the energy breaks it apart and becomes heat instead of reaching the ground. The pieces join up again, ready to absorb more.
asks: Why does the ozone layer stop UV rays?

faq.a: A thinning of the ozone layer over Antarctica each spring, caused mainly by chlorine from man-made chemicals called CFCs. Scientists reported it in 1985.
asks: What made the hole in the ozone layer?

faq.a: Yes. The 1987 Montreal Protocol phased out CFCs, and scientists expect the ozone layer to recover to 1980 levels around 2040 over most of the world and around 2066 over Antarctica.
asks: Has the ozone hole been fixed?

faq.a: High in the stratosphere, ozone protects us from ultraviolet light. Near the ground, ozone made from traffic and factory pollution is harmful to breathe, so it depends where it is.

facts: Most of the ozone layer lies 15 to 35 kilometres above the ground.
The Montreal Protocol, agreed in 1987, became the first UN treaty ratified by every country in the world.

quiz.say: What did the Montreal Protocol phase out to protect the ozone layer?
quiz.why: CFCs released chlorine high in the stratosphere that destroyed ozone, so the treaty phased them out.

wrong.1: Coal burning causes other problems, like carbon dioxide and smog, but was not the target of the ozone treaty.
wrong.2: Plastic bags pollute land and sea but do not destroy ozone.
